chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man upon whom confusion frequently occurs in salat (prayer), so he doubts regarding the rukuʿ, not knowing whether he bowed or not, and he doubts regarding the sujud, not knowing whether he prostrated or not—so he said: He should not prostrate nor bow; rather, he should continue in his salat (prayer) until he becomes certain with certainty.

So this report bears two possibilities: one of them is that he doubts after having entered into another state, and he does not remember with certainty having omitted the bowing or the prostration; then he ought to continue in his salat (prayer) according to what we explained previously. The second is that it is specific to one upon whom forgetfulness frequently occurs, so he was given concession to continue in his salat (prayer) as a facilitation, because the forgetful person, whenever he prostrates and then doubts, would need to prostrate again and thus would never be free of it; for that reason, he was given concession to continue in it.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) in which these doubts occur
key_terms.الْوَهْمُ: recurring confusion or mistaken doubt during salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَسْتَيْقِنَ: he attains certainty free of doubt
key_terms.يَمْضِي: he continues onward without returning to the doubtful act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who frequently doubts whether he performed rukuʿ or sujud in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling for a person who frequently experiences doubt in salat (prayer), especially regarding rukuʿ and sujud. It explains that such a person should continue the prayer rather than repeatedly returning to doubtful acts, either because the doubt arose after moving to a new state or because a concession is given to one often afflicted by forgetfulness.
